top_module.name: motor_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level safety and transport shell for host-controlled actuation bridging. It exposes compact register access, command request/response handshake, safe actuator output, and fault reporting. It must remain the synthesizable top module and shall not be replaced by a leaf, telemetry, or register-bank module.
top_module.functionality: Implements the complete host-facing supervisory wrapper for an external DoMINO inference service: CSR access, safe configuration, request capture, request sequencing, outstanding-transaction tracking, timeout monitoring, response freshness and sequence validation, safe command clamping, fallback selection, fault latching, and actuator command presentation. The top must accept compact command intent only, reject new requests when outstanding work exists or the service is unsafe/unavailable, and drive a conservative actuator setpoint whenever reset, fallback, timeout, protocol mismatch, stale response, illegal configuration, or invalid command conditions occur.
responsibilities: Provide a compact 32-bit CSR transport window for configuration and status.
Capture cmd_payload only when cmd_valid and cmd_ready are asserted together.
Maintain a monotonic or otherwise updated internal sequence counter per accepted request.
Emit a compact request descriptor suitable for external software/GPU transport, containing only metadata and bounded command intent.
Validate response sequence, freshness, and command range before applying output.
Supervise timeout and stale-command detection using a deterministic counter.
Clamp actuator_setpoint to programmable min/max bounds before driving the output.
Assert fault_flag on protocol mismatch, timeout, stale response, illegal configuration, or invalid actuator command.
Expose current FSM state, outstanding sequence number, last fault reason, and safe-fallback-active status via CSR.
Remain synthesizable and deterministic with only counters, comparators, muxes, and FSM logic.
must_not_drive: Do not drive any geometry, tensor, flow-field, or physics-model ports.
Do not expose bulk payload storage or inferred RAM for model data.
Do not create top-level ports wider than 128 bits.
Do not implement surrogate inference internally.
top_module.reset_behavior: On reset, initialize conservative command limits, clear outstanding request state, deassert validity on non-fallback commands, assert safe fallback active, load a safe default actuator setpoint, clear non-sticky status, and leave sticky fault bits in their reset-cleared state unless policy requires retention across warm reset. The FSM must enter a safe state such as SAFE_FALLBACK or RESET-derived fallback behavior and must not issue new external requests until configuration is valid.
behavior_rules: All writes to CSRs are synchronous.
CSR reads reflect current configuration and status in the same or architecturally defined synchronous manner.

cmd_ready shall deassert whenever a request is outstanding, the module is faulted, the model service is unavailable, configuration is illegal, or the safety supervisor is not in a request-accepting state.
When cmd_valid and cmd_ready are high, capture cmd_payload into internal control registers and increment or otherwise update the sequence counter.
If a request is already outstanding, additional commands shall be rejected or back-pressured until completion or timeout.
A response shall be accepted only if sequence matches the outstanding request, freshness is within the configured timeout window, and the returned command is within configured min/max bounds.
Stale, duplicated, or mismatched responses shall be rejected and shall assert fault_flag.
Timeout monitoring shall increment while a request is outstanding and clear or re-arm upon completion.
Fallback command shall be deterministic and selectable from a small predefined set or a host-programmed conservative value within configured bounds.
actuator_valid may assert only when the output has passed validation and clamping; on fault it shall deassert or remain in documented fallback-valid behavior consistent with safe output policy.
Sticky fault bits remain set until explicitly cleared by CSR write or reset.
The RTL shall not package geometry arrays, STL payloads, pressure fields, flow fields, or tensors; only metadata and bounded command intent are permitted.
The design shall support future external runtime integration with NVIDIA-hosted NIM or ChipLoop GPU worker as a transport endpoint only.

modules.name: csr_block
modules.description: Compact synchronous control/status register block implementing enable, fallback selection, timeout threshold, sequence counter visibility, command min/max limits, status bits, and sticky fault bits. It provides decoded semantic configuration to the safety supervisor and returns current status to the register bus.
modules.functionality: Decodes host register accesses into a small synthesizable CSR set. Stores legal configuration for enable, fallback selection, timeout threshold, min/max command bounds, and fallback command value. Provides synchronous readback of live status including FSM state, outstanding sequence number, last fault reason, safe fallback activity, and sticky faults. Supports explicit sticky fault clearing by CSR write. The block must not expose or store geometry, flow, tensor, or payload data.
responsibilities: Accept compact register transactions from the top-level register access window.
Generate read data that reflects current configuration and status.
Provide decoded semantic control outputs to the safety supervisor.
Latch or clear sticky fault bits under explicit CSR control.
Maintain a small synthesizable stateful register set only.
must_not_drive: Do not drive any top-level actuator pins directly.
Do not infer RAM, FIFO, or payload storage.
Do not implement physics or model inference.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset all configuration registers to conservative defaults: enable deasserted or safe-only, fallback select set to a deterministic conservative mode, timeout threshold set to a conservative nonzero value, min/max command bounds initialized to a safe range, fallback value initialized within bounds, and sticky fault clear deasserted. Read data may return zeros or reset defaults until configured.
behavior_rules: CSR writes are synchronous and take effect on the active clock edge.
CSR read data shall be coherent with current stored configuration and status.
Illegal register addresses may return error status and shall not alter protected state.
Sticky fault clear shall only affect sticky bits when explicitly written.
Status inputs shall be sampled and forwarded into the readback map without combinational loops.
Configuration outputs must remain stable between legal writes.
The block shall not create large arrays or memory macros.

modules.name: request_packager
modules.description: Compacts a bounded command intent and sequence metadata into an external-service request descriptor. It does not package geometry arrays, tensors, STL payloads, pressure fields, or flow fields. It only forwards bounded scalar intent for DoMINO-side inference transport.
modules.functionality: Accepts a host command only when enabled, not busy, and not fault-blocked. Captures the bounded command intent, assigns a sequence tag, and emits a compact request descriptor for software/GPU-side transport. The descriptor is metadata-only and bounded; it shall not contain model tensors, geometry arrays, or flow-field data. It provides a request-capture pulse for the safety supervisor and top-level transport logic.
responsibilities: Back-pressure or reject new commands when outstanding work exists or safety policy blocks acceptance.
Increment or otherwise update the sequence number on each accepted command.
Emit a compact descriptor with only bounded scalar intent and metadata.
Support deterministic request formation for external NVIDIA-hosted inference transport.
must_not_drive: Do not drive actuator outputs directly.
Do not emit geometry, tensor, pressure, flow-field, or mesh payloads.
Do not implement external service execution internally.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset output handshake low, descriptor invalid, sequence reset to a deterministic baseline, and ready deasserted until enabled and not blocked. Internal state must not retain stale command intent across reset.
behavior_rules: cmd_ready shall be high only when the module can accept a new request.
When cmd_valid and cmd_ready are asserted, capture cmd_payload into internal control registers and produce a single-cycle capture pulse.
Sequence number shall update deterministically per accepted request.
The emitted descriptor shall be compact, bounded, and suitable only for external transport metadata.
If enabled is low, outstanding_busy is high, or fault_block is high, new requests shall be rejected or back-pressured.
No hidden buffering of bulk data is permitted.

modules.name: response_validator
modules.description: Validates responses from the external DoMINO service against the outstanding request sequence, freshness/timeout window, and programmed safe command range. It rejects stale, duplicated, mismatched, or out-of-range responses and produces a validated command candidate only when all checks pass.
modules.functionality: Performs deterministic response checks: sequence match, freshness within timeout threshold, and command bounds compliance. If any check fails, it raises the corresponding fault indicator and suppresses application of the response. If the response passes validation, it extracts the bounded actuator command candidate for the safety supervisor.
responsibilities: Compare response sequence to the outstanding sequence and expected sequence.
Check response freshness against the configured timeout window.
Check command fields against programmed minimum and maximum bounds.
Suppress invalid responses and raise precise fault indicators.
Provide a validated command only when all checks pass.
must_not_drive: Do not accept or validate tensors, geometry arrays, flow fields, or physics internals.
Do not store bulk histories or payload FIFOs.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset response acceptance low, validation outputs invalid, and fault indicators cleared until a response is observed. The validator must not accept stale data after reset.
behavior_rules: A response is valid only when sequence matches and freshness is within threshold.
Stale, duplicated, or mismatched responses shall be rejected.
Out-of-range responses shall be rejected even if sequence matches.
resp_ready shall reflect the ability to accept response traffic in the current supervisory state.
All checks must be deterministic and synchronous.

modules.name: safety_supervisor
modules.description: Finite-state safety supervisor that arbitrates request issuance, response waiting, validated application, safe fallback, and fault hold. It monitors timeout age, validates configuration legality, selects fallback behavior, clamps actuator commands, and asserts protocol or safety faults on violation.
modules.functionality: Implements the required FSM states RESET, IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, APPLY_VALIDATED_COMMAND, SAFE_FALLBACK, and FAULT_HOLD. It supervises request acceptance, outstanding sequence tracking, timeout counting, response application, conservative fallback selection, and fault latching. On reset or fault it enters safe fallback or fault hold and drives a conservative command. It clamps the actuator command to configured min/max bounds before presenting it downstream.
responsibilities: Own the supervisory state machine and drive safe command policy.
Track outstanding request sequence and clear or re-arm on completion.
Increment or supervise timeout age while a request is outstanding.
Assert fault_flag on timeout, stale response, protocol mismatch, illegal configuration, or invalid actuator command.
Select deterministic fallback command using fallback_select or host-programmed fallback value within bounds.
Clamp validated command to min/max bounds before allowing output.
Report current FSM state, outstanding sequence, last fault reason, and fallback activity.
must_not_drive: Do not directly drive top-level register bus signals.
Do not implement model inference or any geometric/flow computation.
Do not instantiate bulk payload storage or inferred RAM for model data.
modules.reset_behavior: Enter RESET then SAFE_FALLBACK or equivalent conservative behavior on release of reset, clear non-sticky state, initialize outstanding sequence to zero or a safe baseline, deassert command validity except for documented fallback-valid behavior, and drive a conservative actuator setpoint within configured limits. On any fault, transition to FAULT_HOLD or SAFE_FALLBACK per safety policy and keep the system conservative.
behavior_rules: FSM shall include at least RESET, IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, APPLY_VALIDATED_COMMAND, SAFE_FALLBACK, and FAULT_HOLD states.
A request may be issued only when enabled, no fault is active, and no outstanding transaction exists.
Timeout age shall increment while a request is outstanding and shall be compared deterministically to timeout_threshold.
On request completion, timeout monitoring shall clear or re-arm for the next request.
Stale-command detection shall assert fault_flag and block application of the response.
Command clamping shall limit actuator_setpoint to programmed min/max bounds before output.
Safe fallback shall be deterministic and selectable from a small set of predefined conservative poses/commands or a host-programmed conservative value within configured limits.
If configuration is illegal, fault_flag shall assert and the design shall remain in safe fallback or fault hold until corrected or reset.
actuator_valid shall assert only when the command has passed validation and clamping; fallback-valid behavior, if used, must be documented and conservative.

top_level_connections.description: Fan out the single synchronous system clock to all sequential submodules.
Fan out the active-low synchronous reset to all submodules.
Host register request valid is consumed by the CSR block.
Host register write qualifier is consumed by the CSR block.
Compact register address is consumed by the CSR block.
Compact register write data is consumed by the CSR block.
CSR readiness is driven by the CSR block back to the host.
CSR response valid is driven by the CSR block back to the host.
CSR readback data is driven by the CSR block back to the host.
CSR error indication is driven by the CSR block back to the host.
Command valid from the host is consumed by the request packager.
Command ready is generated by the request packager and supervised by the safety state machine for acceptance policy.
Bounded command payload is consumed by the request packager only.
External response valid is consumed by the response validator.
External response ready is driven by the response validator.
External response payload is consumed by the response validator.
Safe, bounded actuator setpoint is driven from the safety supervisor to the top-level actuator output.
Actuator validity is driven from the safety supervisor to the top-level actuator validity output.
Top-level fault flag is driven from the safety supervisor.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_enable
inter_module_signals.description: Decoded enable control from the CSR block to request acceptance and safety supervision.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_fallback_select
inter_module_signals.description: Fallback mode selection from CSR to safety supervisor.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_timeout_threshold
inter_module_signals.description: Programmable timeout threshold for response freshness and timeout supervision.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_cmd_min
inter_module_signals.description: Minimum safe actuator command bound.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_cmd_max
inter_module_signals.description: Maximum safe actuator command bound.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_fallback_value
inter_module_signals.description: Host-programmed conservative fallback command within configured limits.

inter_module_signals.name: request_captured
inter_module_signals.description: Single-cycle capture indication that a new request has been accepted and packaged.

inter_module_signals.name: request_sequence
inter_module_signals.description: Sequence number assigned to the accepted request.

inter_module_signals.name: request_descriptor
inter_module_signals.description: Compact metadata-only request descriptor forwarded for external transport context; no tensors or geometry are included.

inter_module_signals.name: request_descriptor_valid
inter_module_signals.description: Descriptor validity indication to gate external request issuance.

inter_module_signals.name: outstanding_busy
inter_module_signals.description: Busy/back-pressure indication derived from supervisory state to block new requests while a transaction is outstanding or fallback is active.

inter_module_signals.name: fault_block
inter_module_signals.description: Fault block signal preventing new request acceptance under unsafe conditions.

inter_module_signals.name: resp_expected_seq
inter_module_signals.description: Expected response sequence number for validation.

inter_module_signals.name: timeout_age
inter_module_signals.description: Deterministic age counter or age-equivalent supervision input used for freshness checks and timeout management.

inter_module_signals.name: validated_valid
inter_module_signals.description: Indicates that the response passed all validation checks and may be considered for application.

inter_module_signals.name: validated_command
inter_module_signals.description: Validated actuator command candidate forwarded to the safety supervisor for clamping and output selection.

inter_module_signals.name: fault_stale
inter_module_signals.description: Stale response fault indication.

inter_module_signals.name: fault_sequence_mismatch
inter_module_signals.description: Sequence mismatch fault indication.

inter_module_signals.name: fault_range_violation
inter_module_signals.description: Out-of-range response fault indication.

inter_module_signals.name: fsm_state
inter_module_signals.description: Current supervisory FSM state for CSR status reporting.

inter_module_signals.name: outstanding_seq
inter_module_signals.description: Outstanding request sequence number for CSR status reporting.

inter_module_signals.name: last_fault_reason
inter_module_signals.description: Last recorded fault reason for CSR status reporting.

inter_module_signals.name: safe_fallback_active
inter_module_signals.description: Indicates whether conservative fallback is currently active.

inter_module_signals.name: fault_sticky
inter_module_signals.description: Sticky fault summary for CSR status reporting.

inter_module_signals.name: actuator_setpoint_int
inter_module_signals.description: Bounded internal actuator setpoint driven to the top-level output.

inter_module_signals.name: actuator_valid_int
inter_module_signals.description: Validated internal actuator-valid flag driven to the top-level output.

registers.name: CTRL_ENABLE
registers.description: Global enable for request acceptance and active supervision.

registers.name: CTRL_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD
registers.description: Timeout window in cycles for outstanding request freshness.

registers.name: CTRL_FALLBACK_VALUE
registers.description: Host-programmed conservative fallback command within bounds.

registers.name: STATUS_SAFE_FALLBACK_ACTIVE
registers.description: Indicates whether safe fallback is active.
